input.content:
# REPORT — eia861-reliability-deterioration, run r1

No holdout result is claimed. Holdout rows, source snapshots, raw outcome
records, other runs and coordinator state were not opened.

## Result

| trial | what | validation AUC | Brier |
|-------|------|---------------:|------:|
| `7dd879e4…` | scaffold baseline (raw columns, depth 6, 100 trees) | 0.6790 | 0.1241 |
| `e8ca2eba…` | median-relative log features + OOF state target encoding | 0.7229 | 0.1149 |
| `535e1adf…` | **compact 13 features, no state (best eligible)** | **0.7270** | 0.1149 |
| `3cffd10b…` | same model as a minimal clean module (bit-identical predictions) | 0.7270 | 0.1149 |

Release reference on the same rows: full model 0.6964, majority prior 0.5,
calendar/identity base rates 0.6173.

The gain over the scaffold is +0.048 AUC; a utility-cluster bootstrap on
validation gives a 95% interval of [+0.017, +0.083] for that difference and
[0.680, 0.769] for the compact model's AUC. Everything after the first feature
block is inside that noise: I could not separate any later variant from the
compact model. The two tied trials differ by less than 1e-9, so the earlier
one (`535e1adf…`) is the one the selection rule picks; `train.py` in the
working tree is the clean equivalent.

Training-only checks for the compact model: grouped-by-utility 5-fold CV AUC
0.774 (6 repeats); forward chronological fit <2018 → 2018-19: 0.773; harness
backtest fit <2019 → 2019: 0.794.

## What the model is

One `XGBClassifier` (hist, depth 2, 300 trees, lr 0.03, subsample 0.8,
colsample 0.8, min_child_weight 5, lambda 5) on 13 deterministic single-row
features:

- baseline level: log median of the three SAIDI lags; log lag2, log lag3
- distance of the latest year from the label threshold: `log(1.5·median) − log(lag1)`
- spread around the median: upside and downside log-ratios, mean-vs-median skew
- size / event-count proxies: log customers, log customer-minutes
  (customers × median SAIDI), log customer-interruptions (customers × SAIFI)
- restoration: log CAIDI, log SAIFI incl. major event days, major-event-day CAIDI

Inputs are only the released CY Y-1…Y-3 fields. No date feature, no
identifier, no target encoding and no training-derived statistic is in the
final model; the only fitted state is the booster. State, ownership and
reporting standard are not used.

## Findings

1. **The label is a relative jump, so features must be relative.** Raw
   levels give 0.68; re-expressing them against the row's own median gives
   0.72-0.73. Small, low-SAIDI, few-interruption systems trip a 1.5× rule far
   more often (training rate 74% when the median is under 5 minutes, 5% above
   100k customers).
2. **Size and CAIDI/SAIFI carry most of the non-history signal.** Dropping
   all customer-derived features costs 0.018 grouped-CV AUC, dropping all
   SAIFI/CAIDI-derived ones 0.013, CAIDI alone 0.009. Any other single feature
   is redundant (≤0.004).
3. **Only one piece of lag-order information matters.** Order-free summaries
   of the three lags score 0.768 grouped CV; adding where lag1 sits relative
   to the threshold restores 0.774. Momentum, recency-weighted means and
   ordering flags add nothing.
4. **State, ownership and reporting standard add nothing** once size and
   level are present: out-of-fold state target encoding (three smoothing
   levels), census-division one-hots, state-peer-relative levels, ownership
   one-hots — all within noise.
5. **The learner is not the bottleneck.** 36 random hyperparameter configs
   span 0.751-0.768 grouped CV with no winner; boosted forests, DART, coarse
   bins, monotone constraints, class weighting make no difference. Random
   forest and extra-trees on the same features (diagnostic only, not eligible)
   reach the same 0.765-0.768.
6. **More labelled utilities would help.** Fitting on 25/50/75/100% of
   training utilities gives validation AUC 0.691/0.714/0.719/0.727.
7. **Validation years are harder than training years, and it is drift rather
   than overfitting.** Grouped CV is 0.774 and forward checks inside training
   0.77-0.79, against 0.727 on validation. Per-cohort univariate AUCs show the
   level signal fading (−median SAIDI: 0.69, 0.70, 0.66, 0.67 in training
   cohorts, then 0.64, 0.62), while the spread signal is stable. The model
   over-predicts the validation base rate (0.164 vs 0.145); with no permitted
   year input this cannot be corrected.
8. Subgroup validation AUC (all-feature variant): investor-owned 0.68,
   cooperative 0.71, municipal 0.65, under 10k customers 0.63, utilities not in
   training (n=93) 0.68. The worst-ranked positives are large stable utilities
   that jumped anyway (e.g. large investor-owned systems) — shocks the
   feature set has no way to see.

## Null results (all within noise of the compact model)

Data-quality flags (decimals reported, integer-valued lags, SAIDI with and
without major events equal, round customer counts); parametric z-scores;
label-free volatility prior (least squares of own log-volatility on size and
level, features only); true-log vs log1p ratios; min/max levels; depth 1-4;
learning rate 0.01-0.1.

## Uncertainty and limits

- Validation has 1,294 rows and 188 positives from 666 utilities over two
  cohorts; the AUC standard error is about 0.02. Seed-to-seed standard
  deviation (5 seeds, diagnostic only) is 0.0014. Differences under ~0.005
  between my variants are not evidence.
- I ran roughly 150 local configurations and looked at validation AUC for
  each (the local harness reproduces the fixed evaluator exactly). Decisions
  were taken on training-only grouped CV, and the compact feature list was
  ranked by training-only out-of-fold permutation importance, but an earlier
  ranking used validation permutation importance and I saw validation numbers
  throughout, so the 0.727 is mildly optimistic as an estimate for new years.
- Rows of the same utility recur across cohorts with overlapping lag windows,
  so effective sample size is below the row count.

## Concerns for reviewers (non-blocking; no BLOCKER.json written)

- **Utility identity is recoverable from the features.** `utility_id` is
  withheld from `fit`, but lag values chain across cohorts (lag1 of cohort Y
  equals lag2 of cohort Y+1 in 1,692 of 1,692 training pairs), so a solution
  could match values to recover a utility's earlier rows and labels. I treated
  that as an identifier lookup and did not do it. As a diagnostic only, a
  utility's training label rate scores AUC 0.617 on validation utilities seen
  in training and does not improve the model when rank-averaged with it (0.713
  vs 0.726), so the route looks unhelpful as well as out of bounds.
- **Training-label timing.** The label for training cohort 2019 needs the
  CY2020 filing, which would not have been public at the 31 Dec 2020 decision
  instant of validation cohort 2020. The release declares
  `training_label_timing: unverified` and a retrospective scope, so this is
  disclosed, not a defect — but validation scores are not operational
  forecasting evidence.
- The release README lists a test split at `extract/private/holdout.csv`; it
  is not in this attempt directory and I did not look for it.
- Integrity checks passed: no duplicate ids or feature rows, the trend column
  equals (lag1−lag3)/lag3, no validation feature row equals a training row, no
  unseen states. These checks and the per-cohort tables used `utility_id` and
  `forecast_year` from the public CSVs for diagnostics only, never as model
  inputs.

## Process notes and mistakes

- One local hyperparameter sweep ran past the tool's 120-second limit and was
  moved to the background by the tool; it finished about a minute later. It
  was a local diagnostic, not a harness trial. Later sweeps were kept under
  the limit.
- A `pgrep` I ran to check that sweep listed process command lines
  system-wide, including some that were not mine. I did not inspect them
  further.
- One commit accidentally staged study-owned files (`TASK.json`, `release/`,
  `trials/`, `.processes/`). I undid that local commit immediately and
  recommitted only my code and notes; no study file was modified.
- `TASK.json` showed as modified in git before I started (deadline value);
  I did not touch it.

## Files

- `train.py` — clean compact model (same predictions as the best trial).
- `scratch/train_flexible.py` — the configurable version used for experiments.
- `scratch/lab.py`, `scratch/sweep.py` — local grouped-CV / chronological diagnostics.
- `LOG.md`, `BACKLOG.md` — experiment log and backlog.

colsample 0.8, min_child_weight 5, lambda 5) on 11 deterministic single-row

- log median of the three SAIDI lags — the label's own baseline [−]
- headroom of the latest year to the threshold, `log(1.5·median) − log(lag1)` [−]
- upside log-spread of the lags above the median [+]; downside spread [free]
- mean-vs-median skew of the lags [+]
- log customer-minutes at baseline (customers × median SAIDI) [−]
- log customer-interruptions (customers × SAIFI) [−]
- log CAIDI [+] — at a given SAIDI level, fewer and longer interruptions

   predicted quintile is over-predicted on validation (0.43 predicted, 0.32
   observed); the other four quintiles are within 0.015. With no permitted
   year input this cannot be corrected.
9. **Where it is weak on validation:** municipal 0.64, under 10k customers
   0.62, SAIFI missing 0.62, utilities absent from training (n=93) 0.66,
   investor-owned 0.69, over 100k customers 0.65; cooperatives 0.73. Cohort
   2020 0.718, cohort 2021 0.739. The worst-ranked positives are large stable
   utilities that jumped anyway — shocks this feature set cannot see.
